prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you parallel-parked a full-size pickup on the first attempt and were observed being proud about it. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the Cookout Division.

I appear before this committee today not to evade, but to clarify. I understand the gravity of these allegations. In these uncertain times, when the integrity of our nation’s tailgates and backyard gatherings hangs in the balance, any display of unearned confidence is rightly viewed with suspicion. I respect this committee’s vigilance.

However, I must respectfully but firmly contest the characterization of my actions as "being proud."

What the witness observed on the afternoon of July 4th was not pride, sir. It was *relief*. There is a profound difference. Pride implies a sense of superiority, an arrogance unbecoming of a citizen who understands that parallel parking a full-size pickup is a privilege, not a right. What I felt was merely the quiet, trembling gratitude of a driver who had checked their mirrors, accounted for the curb, and avoided the catastrophic social fallout of a three-point turn in front of the neighbors.

Furthermore, I wish to address the allegation regarding the "first attempt." I submit for the record that this was not a display of reckless natural talent or un-American ease. It was the product of decades of disciplined practice, spatial anxiety, and a deep-seated fear of scratching the host’s fence. To call it effortless is to ignore the sweat on the steering wheel and the white-knuckled grip of a citizen doing their duty to keep the flow of charcoal traffic moving.

If my momentary exhale of breath was mistaken for a smirk, I apologize. If my efficient use of available curb space was interpreted as a subversive act of individualism, I assure you it was only in service of getting the cooler unloaded before the ice melted.

I have no un-American parking agenda. I yield my spot willingly when asked, I signal my intentions clearly, and I pledge my allegiance to the double-parked sedan of liberty.

Thank you, Mr. Chairman. I am prepared to answer any further questions, or to demonstrate my technique under committee supervision, should you deem it necessary for national security.
